segments.text: Good afternoon, this is Aakash Vani and I am Saira Muchthaba with the Midday News.

And now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India will definitely fulfil its dream of becoming
a developed nation by 2047 through visionary policies and hard work.
Addressing the Vikasit Bharat Sankal Sabha in New Delhi today, Mr. Modi said that present
governments policy focuses on solutions for all citizens.
He said India, once associated with discussions on policy paralysis, is now increasingly
being discussed for its growing strength and resilience.

noted that earlier efforts were made to increase imports while today Inter is setting new export
records. He said that the decade from 2015 to 2025 witnessed the highest sustained agricultural
growth since independence, surpassing all previous records. Mr Modi said that such
transformation is possible when the intent is clear and policies are well-defined.
The Prime Minister also said that this is the time to set big targets for Bharat.
Attributing his entire political journey to the unwavering faith and support of the citizens,
Mr Modi said that the present government's policy focuses on solutions for all citizens.
Her minister Amit Shah today hailed the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's
public service and described it as a golden and historic day.
Addressing the Vikasiddh Bharat Sankat Sabha, Seva Jyoti Yatra in Gurugram today, he stated
that under Prime Minister Modi's leadership, significant work was accomplished including
including the abrogation of Article 370, the elimination of noctilism, and the elevation
of the country's infrastructure to the highest level.
He mentioned that as part of this campaign, torch light processions are being organized
during which young people will take out a seva jyoti yatra and install the torch at
the designated crossing.
Mr. Shah Urjh everyone to join the yatra in as large numbers as possible.
Whenever the history of India is written, these 25 years will be written in golden letters.
These 25 years have seen freedom from poverty, or secure India, abrogation of Article 370,
the end of Naxalism, construction of the Ramjan Mahbhoomi and Kashi Vishwanath temples, infrastructure
being taken to unprecedented levels, and 25 crore poor people being lifted above the
poverty line.
25 crore poor people should be raised from the poverty line."
External Affairs Minister Dr. Air Jay Shankar has said that India's partnership with Africa
is being built not just for today, but for generations to come.
Addressing a gathering at the Foreign Service Institute of Ghana in Accra, he said diplomacy
must manage competition without allowing it to turn into confrontation and promote
cooperation despite differences in interest.
years. Dr. Jay Shankar highlighted India's progress in the economy, infrastructure, digital
technology and manufacturing. He stressed the need for India and Africa to turn their
young populations into skilled and empowered citizens.
After nearly three-and-a-half years, the Reserve Bank of India RBI today raised the
key benchmark policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent, in a bid to contain rising
inflation amid continuing global and geopolitical uncertainties. The last
reparate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25% to 6.5%.
It kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24, before beginning its rate cut cycle in 2025.
Announcing the bi-monthly monetary policy, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said,
said, the Monetary Policy Committee unanimously decided to raise the policy reparate by 25
basis points.
After a detailed assessment of the evolving macroeconomic and financial conditions, developments
and the outlook the MPC voted unanimously to increase the policy reparate under the
LAF by 25 basis points to 5.5%. Consequently, the STF rate stands adjusted at 5.25% and
the marginal standing facility rate and the bank rate to 5.75%. The MPC also decided to
change the stance to calibrated tightening by a majority of 42.
The RBI also projected real GDP growth for the current financial year at 7.1%. With growth
projected at 7.2% in the second quarter, 6.9% in the third quarter and 6.8% in the
fourth quarter. Arvia has raised its inflation projection for financial year to 5.2% from
5.1% earlier. Inflation is projected at 4.9% in the second quarter, 6% in the third quarter
and 5.7% in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, retail inflation rose to 4.8% in August
compared to 4.45% in the previous month. This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Welcome back to Biddy News. NFIR has been registered by Delhi Police against Congress leaders Rahul
Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi-Vadra on trespassing charges for entering Akashwani Bhavan in New
Delhi during yesterday's protest march. The FIR under relevant sections has been registered
at Parliament Street Police Station, and an investigation has already started. Yesterday,
several MPs of the opposition India block had called for a protest march from Makardwar
of Parliament to the Election Commission headquarters. The march led by Congress
leader Rahul Gandhi was stopped near Akash Rani Bhavan. After that, the Congress leaders entered
Akash Rani Bhavan and staged a sit-in there. Delhi Traffic Police has issued a traffic advisory
in view of the proposed demonstration at the office of the Delhi's chief electoral officer today
from 12 noon to 3.30 pm. It said that traffic movement in and around Kashmiri
Gate area is likely to be affected. The traffic police advised commuters to avoid
avoid affected stretches, plan their journeys in advance, use alternate routes, and follow
the directions of Delhi Traffic Police personnel.
India has called for stronger climate action and faster implementation of the progress
agreement at the pre-COV-31 meeting in Fiji.
Union Environment Minister Bupindari Adhav said,
There is a need to close gaps in understanding, fulfil existing climate commitments, and accelerate
progress towards the goal of limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius.
years. Addressing the plenary session, Mr. Yadav stressed the need for greater capacity
building and adequate means of implementation. He called for concrete examples of high-impact
climate mitigation, large-scale adaptation and effective delivery of climate finance
and other resources.
We have seen that there can't be one-size-fits-all pathway to climate action. As we move towards
COP31, India believes that adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation must receive
equity, equal attention and the key principle of equity, common but differentiated responsibilities
and respective capabilities, upheld in the latter in its fate for meaningful and sustained

India has rejected the Organization of Islamic Co-operations or OIC's remarks on Jammu and
Kashmir and India's actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan.
Speaking at the UN General Assembly Sixth Committee, Lok Sabha MP Bipla Kumar Dev said those
making the remarks were unable to distinguish between the victim and the perpetrator. He
asserted that India has the right to defend its people against cross-border terrorism emanating
from Pakistan. IMF Managing Director Kristelina Georgieva has
called on countries both rich and poor to take faster action to reduce debt and tackle
growing inequality. Speaking in Singapore ahead of the IMF World Bank meetings in
Bangkok next week, she said governments have the tools to address economic challenges
issues, but need to take necessary policy decisions without further delay.
She also highlighted risks from the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence, including
heavy investment in data centers, rising energy demand, and potential financial shocks if
AI-related earnings fall short of expectations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desheva, and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving the goal of a vikasit Bharat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming
lives.
Today in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been
translated into action through the Lakpati Didi Yojna.
The government is implementing the Lakpati Didi scheme with the objective of economically
powering women in rural areas and increasing their income.
The initiative aims to enable women associated with self-help groups to earn at least 1 lakh
rupees annually through various sustainable livelihood activities.
Women are being provided with facilities such as skilled development training, financial
assistance, access to credit, guidance for entrepreneurship, and linkages with markets.
The Prime Minister has said that the target is now to create 6 crore Lakhpati Didis across the country.
We have crossed the goal of making 3 crore sisters Lakhpati Didi.
Now we are moving ahead with the goal of making 6 crore Lakhpati Didi.
3 crore new Lakhpati Didi means a big change in the world.

Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura during the day.
After the mid-department of Himachal Pradesh issued a yellow alert, the weather today has
taken a turn once again.
snowfall is occurring in the state's high-altitude mountainous regions while other areas are experiencing
thunderstorms and rain, more from our correspondent.
Due to the activity of a western disturbance, the weather in Yamachupradesh has shifted.
High-altitude areas are witnessing snowfall while lower regions are experiencing hailstorms
and thunderstorms accompanied by rain. There are also apprehensions of damage to crops.
This precipitation has led to a drop in temperatures and an increase in the chill.
Snowfall has occurred on the high peaks of Lahore-Spiti, Pangi and Kullu, while the high
peaks of P.Panjal Range, including the Rothang Pass, are now draped in a blanket of snow.
According to the meteorological centre in Shimla, a yellow alert has been issued for thunderstorms
and lightning in the district of Una, Bilaspur, Hamirpur, Kangra, Mandi, Shimla and Solan
for the next four days, while light snowfall is expected in Kullu and Lahore-Spiti, with
Ritesh Kapoor's report, Jigasa Pandey, Akash Mani News.
